clue.text: Clean hit to leg.

definitions.meaning: to clean a floor or chimney is to brush it out with a broom
in cricket, a stroke played on one knee, swinging the ball round to the leg side

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs; this stroke is played kneeling and swung across.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: brushing a room clean, and the cricket stroke that sends the ball to the leg side.

clue.text: In which performance ankle was broken?

definitions.text: In which performance ankle was broken?

indicators.note: broken means the letters of ankle and was are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A ballet performance during which a dancer broke an ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous Tchaikovsky ballet, a performance in which dancers could break an ankle.

clue.text: Failure of Oval tail is shown as a series of dots

indicators.note: failure of a part means that part is missing and is dropped
the tail is the final letter, the one that fails

parts.note: an ellipse is an oval shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket ground's tail-end batters fail and are shown as dots on the scorecard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which suggests a batting collapse; here it is a flattened circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots marking an omission in writing are this punctuation mark.

clue.text: After testing water with toe, make mistaken further commitment?

definitions.text: After testing water with toe, make mistaken further commitment?

parts.words: After testing water with toe, make mistaken further commitment?
parts.note: having dipped a toe in, a bather wrongly commits the whole lower limb; idiomatically, to make a tactless blunder

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to blunder tactlessly, here pictured literally as plunging a limb into the water after a toe test.

clue.text: Films the best baseball player

parts.note: short films are called shorts
the top is the best, as in 'top of the class'

explanation.surface: A movie fan names the finest player in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder positioned between second and third base in baseball has this name.

clue.text: Dispatch saint to martyrdom

parts.note: martyrdom is the end of a martyr's life

explanation.surface: A saint is dispatched to die for the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something is to dispatch it.

clue.text: Began to accept notice without prejudice

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something that began has opened
to mind is to notice or heed

explanation.surface: Someone started to heed a warning, free from bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Being receptive to new ideas and unbiased is being free of prejudice.

clue.text: Book a holiday on the Thames

definitions.meaning: a comic novel of 1889 by Jerome K Jerome
a boating trip up the river, the novel's subject, pictured as a holiday for a trio of friends afloat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as the verb to reserve; it is a noun, the title of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K Jerome's comic novel recounts three friends and a dog on a rowing holiday up the River Thames.

clue.text: Workers organised to read Italian

parts.note: workers organised into a body form a trade union, abbreviated TU
to scan a page is to read it

explanation.surface: Union members are set up to study Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Tuscany is Italian; the regional adjective stands for an Italian.

clue.text: Starfish

parts.note: not a sea creature but fish in the stars: the zodiac sign and constellation of the fishes

explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac constellation is represented by two fish, so it is a star fish.

clue.text: How Wordsworth saw his host, without warning

definitions.meaning: a line of the daffodils poem: 'When ... I saw a crowd, / A host, of golden daffodils'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a party host, but in Wordsworth's 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud' it is a crowd of daffodils.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means suddenly, and is exactly how the poet says he came upon the host of daffodils.

clue.text: Is sorry about son's tricks

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around another

parts.note: to rue something is to be sorry about it, so 'is sorry' gives rues
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the deceptions their boy has pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RUES around S; the 's on son is just the possessive, no extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are cunning stratagems, which is what tricks are.

clue.text: Roused in row, like a wild animal

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: a row of things is a line
someone roused from bed is up

explanation.surface: Someone stirred up in a quarrel behaves like a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel, but it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means wolflike, and the wolf is the wild animal in question.

clue.text: A Parliamentarian's anger against European leads to current measure

indicators.note: against means next to, so the two pieces lean on each other side by side

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
rage is anger

explanation.surface: An MP's fury at Europe leads to a new measure being brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current measure' sounds like a policy now in force, but it is the strength of an electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical current is measured in amps, and the total measured is this quantity.

clue.text: Bishop died during lots of bad weather, such a loss of talent

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: during means inside the span of, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: lots of rain, so the word rain comes twice

explanation.surface: A bishop passed away in a long spell of wet weather, a sad loss of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts D inside RAINRAIN; 'lots of' doubles the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the emigration of skilled people, which is a loss of talent to the country.

clue.text: Say, dock spaniel and provide a little jumper

indicators.note: say tells us the first piece is how a word sounds when spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to dock a tail is to clip it
a springer is a breed of spaniel

explanation.surface: Trim the dog's tail and give the child a small sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater; it is a leaping animal. 'and provide' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: This small African antelope is famous for leaping nimbly among rocks, so it is a little jumper.

clue.text: I protest violently appearing to have worsening measles

indicators.note: violently signals the letters are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loudly objects to looking increasingly blotchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles getting worse makes a patient more covered in spots, a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Was in the aisles, almost, taken by subtle jest

indicators.note: taken by means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: dry humour is subtle and understated

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an audience laughing hard rolled in the aisles

explanation.surface: Someone laughing in the aisles is caught by a subtle joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was in the aisles' is the theatre idiom 'rolled in the aisles', laughing helplessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is whimsical humour, and a jest is a piece of it.

clue.text: Sort of tear-jerkin' historical romance?

parts.note: read 'tear-jerkin'' not as tearjerking but as tearing a jerkin, a close-fitting garment, which is what happens in a racy costume novel

explanation.definitionFit: The term names a steamy historical novel in which a heroine's tight top garment gets torn.

clue.text: Easily persuaded one to enter factory

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a factory is a plant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gullible person is talked into joining a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pliant is flexible and yielding, so easily persuaded.

clue.text: Powerful aria inhibits tenor extremely

indicators.note: inhibits means holds in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: an aria is a song

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters of tenor

explanation.surface: A mighty aria holds the tenor back to the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerful and strong are synonyms.

clue.text: Tolerance of sententious remark not evident at first

indicators.note: the first letter is not to be seen, so it is removed

parts.note: a platitude is a trite moralising remark

explanation.surface: Patience with someone's preachy pronouncement wears thin before it shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom or leeway allowed, which is a form of tolerance.

clue.text: They fix prices shown in pounds on menu

indicators.note: on means placed after in a down or across reading, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: the carte is the menu, as in 'a la carte'
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A restaurant's prices are set in pounds on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms colluding to fix prices, and 'they' stands for that collective body.

clue.text: Country used to have Conservative as leader

indicators.note: as leader puts this piece at the front

parts.note: had is the past form of have

explanation.surface: A nation formerly had a Tory at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is an African country.

clue.text: Potentially tree shows a grain

parts.note: corn is grain

explanation.surface: A seed that could be a tree displays a grain pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak's seed nut has the potential to become a tree.

clue.text: Making new settlement, adopt heir who inspires love

indicators.note: making a new settlement of letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: In a new legal settlement, someone adopts an heir out of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' suggests a legal or financial deal; here it signals a rearrangement of ADOPT HEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of love, so she is the one who inspires love.

clue.text: Screwed up, get hit — end in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disordered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous wreck gets beaten and ends up in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' looks like messed up or anxious; it means turned tight, as a screw is. 'in trouble' rearranges GET HIT END.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw turned home has been made tighter, so screwed up means drawn tighter.

clue.text: Slow these days, to be regularly involved in touchdown

annotationWithheld.why: Slow these days, to be regularly involved in touchdown: AD (these days) is interleaved letter by letter with TRY (touchdown) to give T-A-R-D-Y; the grammar has no interleave operation, and ins() cannot split AD across two positions
annotationWithheld.clue: Slow these days, to be regularly involved in touchdown
